name: Mixlings!
lang: English, Italian, Spanish - Spain, Indonesian, Japanese, Thai, Simplified Chinese, Spanish - Latin America, Vietnamese, Arabic, Korean, Malay
short: What?! Desktop idle game with thousands of cards! Build your adventure team. Mixlings auto-fight monsters, idle with friends for casual fun. Fuse two cards to make unique Mixlings with surprising looks & stats. Every fusion yields unexpected new cards. Create your Mixlings team!
about: Welcome to Mixlings! — a wonderful world where you can create new life again and again!        Tens of thousands of cards, and perhaps even more, are waiting for you to build your team and explore a lost world! But here's something you should know: in Mixlings!, every little companion you meet might be created just for you by AI.   It all started with Dr. Sweetie...        In a post-apocalyptic world overrun by mutated garbage monsters, civilization has collapsed and countless species have vanished. Dr. Sweetie, one of the survivors, has been working tirelessly to find a solution. Then one day, a crazy idea popped into her head: What would happen if you combined a Battle Chicken with a Tank Pig? They have completely different appearances, traits, and abilities. So Dr. Sweetie began experimenting with mixing different companions. Battle Chicken + Tank Pig! Baby Fire Dragon + Speedy Bunny! And what if you mixed two newly created companions together AGAIN?   You probably don't know the answer.            And that's perfectly fine, because Dr. Sweetie probably doesn't know either! AI will create an entirely new Mixling based on the companions you choose to mix. It might inherit a bunny's ears, a pig's tail, or suddenly grow something completely unexpected! It might be adorable, handsome, round and squishy, or so incredibly weird that you start questioning what on earth you and Dr. Sweetie have created!  But none of that matters. The most important thing is — it belongs to you, and quite possibly ONLY to you!  You are the Master of Mixlings! Mix after mix, you'll discover companions you've never seen before. You can even combine two of your weirdest creations to see what comes out next! Your collection will grow from a handful of ordinary little Mixlings into a huge family filled with extraordinary creatures. Create new life for this broken world, and use your creations to save those still suffering under the rule of the garbage monsters!  Of course, you're not creating these little guys just to admire them in your collection.   Pick your favorite Mixlings and assemble your very own adventure squad!           Your Mixlings will hop aboard their vehicle and set off into the unknown. They'll automatically battle enemies, encounter monsters, challenge Bosses, and bring back valuable resources and materials. Every Mixling has its own unique strengths. Who's going to stand in front and take all the hits? (Nobody volunteers? Haha!) Who's dealing the damage? (Probably the one with the worst temper!) And who's going to hide in the back and quietly help out? (Wait... is that YOU?) You can carefully plan the perfect team composition, or simply throw all your favorite little weirdos together — because cuteness IS combat power!  And when you're working, studying, or simply leaving the game running in a corner of your desktop, the adventure doesn't stop.   1Build your team, sit back, and let them do their thing!           Your little Mixlings will keep themselves busy: fighting monsters, moving forward, and collecting loot. Check back occasionally, and you might discover they've traveled surprisingly far and brought home piles of goodies! But even more importantly, they might have rescued some of the original Mixlings along the way!  Of course, your Mixlings aren't the only companions you'll have on this journey. Your real friends can join the adventure too! Team up with your friends and enjoy idle adventures together. Playing together doesn't just dramatically increase your combat power. It also adds more minecart carriages, giving your team extra space to carry even more loot! But teamwork isn't the whole story. Because in Mixlings!, there's a little competition too!   And that competition comes in the form of DICE!           Roll the dice and let fate decide who gets those precious treasures! Sure, your friends might snatch away an item you've been dreaming of. But hey, don't worry! The rewards of working together are still far greater tha

name: CozyDuck Idle
lang: English, Simplified Chinese, Turkish
short: A cozy idle farm that lives in a small window on your screen. Duck workers harvest, haul and sell your crops while you work or play. Grow the farm, open the Duck Pond, earn Heirloom Seeds and dress your ducks in hats and bows.
about: Your farm, in the corner of your screen        CozyDuck Idle runs in a small borderless window that stays on top of everything else. Put it next to your browser, your spreadsheet or your game, and let the ducks do the work. Drag it anywhere, peek over now and then, and spend what they've earned. The ducks run the farm        Every coin gets there on duck feet. Farmer ducks harvest into their baskets, the truck hauls boxes to the barn, and the shop duck sells them. lang: English, Japanese, Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese, French, German, Spanish - Spain, Russian, Portuguese - Brazil, Korean, Italian
short: Pebble to Star is an idle growth game. Swallow the bodies that drift past and raise a grey pebble into a planet, a star, even a black hole and a galaxy, immersed in an ever-changing universe.
about: Pebble to Star is an idle growth game.  Pull in the bodies that drift past and raise a grey pebble into the world you want: a planet, a star, a black hole, a galaxy.  You start as a grey rock in a 1-bit sky. Nothing is timed. What you eat decides what you become.      Left-click to pull, right-click to push  Left-click a comet or a meteor and it falls in, leaving a crater. Hold the left button and sweep to take whatever the cursor passes. Right-click what you don't want and it is flung away. Anything flashing red is on a collision course: take it, or push it off. The heavier you grow, the more your gravity pulls in by itself, and it keeps eating while you are away.              Become the world you want  Open the growth route and pick a destination: an ocean world, an iron planet, a blue giant, a magnetar. A checklist in the corner shows what is still missing. Ice makes oceans and metal makes iron worlds; the mass you ignite at decides what kind of star you become, and how heavy it is when it dies decides what it leaves behind.              From 1-bit to 24-bit  The screen starts in 1-bit black and white. As heat, water and life build up and you grow from layer to layer, it gains color depth bit by bit, until oceans, clouds, rings and nebulae show in full color.              Events ask you to choose  A neighboring planet swings past: move inward, move outward, or hold your orbit. The Sun falls toward you: merge, or push it away. A planetary embryo the size of Mars is aimed at you: a grazing hit makes a moon, and melts the whole surface. Every layer brings choices like these, all the way up to colliding galaxies.              A civilization, from first light to last  Keep a living world stable and a civilization appears: you can see its lights. Then it reaches outward: telescopes, satellites, a space station, starships. But one big impact throws it back into a dark age, or ends it and leaves only ruins.              In the game:   Grow     Grow from a pebble all the way to a galaxy, with a new look and new events at every stage    Dozens of destinations: worlds, stars, stellar remnants and galaxies, each with its own conditions    A star map with dozens of upgrades across several branches, bought with the elements you eat    Several kinds of life, and more than one way for a civilization to leave its planet    The first cloud, the first rain, the first city lights: these firsts slow down so you can see them     A real universe     Modeled on current astrophysical theory and observations: stars die the way real stars do, almost every event is based on a real object, and the black hole is ray-traced through curved spacetime    Overview: pull back to see your whole planetary system, and how big you are next to the Moon, the Sun and the Milky Way     Collect and start again     A codex of 100+ worlds and phenomena, and an in-game camera for the moments you want to keep    If you like collecting: fill the codex and the periodic table    Every run ends with a poster of everything you became, saved to your album    Big Bounce: collapse the universe and start again with a periodic table that keeps your progress    Complete the periodic table and you can refuse the bounce: watch the universe age all the way to heat death     Play your way     Let it grow on its own: switch on idle and it keeps eating while you are away; growing up waits for you. Sometimes letting go is a choice too    Wallpaper mode: put your planet on your Windows desktop and watch it grow while you do other things    Controller and Steam Deck support        How far can your pebble grow?

lang: English, Japanese, Simplified Chinese*, Korean*
short: A Three Kingdoms idle loot game on your desktop. Let heroes march and fight while you do your thing. Collect gear, reroll affixes, build your squad, and set auto-retreat by health, loot-bag capacity, or waves. Take command and challenge the bosses of the Three Kingdoms!
about: A Three Kingdoms-themed desktop idle loot game. Keep your squad in a corner of your screen while you work, watch videos, or do your own thing. Your heroes will keep marching and fighting. When you have a moment, check what dropped and figure out how to make your squad stronger.   Automatic Combat—Get On with Your Day  Pick your heroes, equip their gear, and let the squad head out on its own. From ordinary troops to bosses across the Three Kingdoms, keep pushing while you can. Hit a wall? Come back, change your gear, and try again.         Three Kingdoms Heroes—Find Your Own Strategy  Who takes the hits? Who deals the damage? Who keeps everyone going? Choose your heroes and allocate their attributes your way. Try different combinations and put together a three-hero squad that feels right for you.         Gear and Affixes—Something to Look Forward To  Multiple equipment slots give you plenty of room to experiment. When a new item drops, do you equip it right away or save it for another hero? Even one well-chosen affix could help a struggling squad push through a few more waves.         Customize Your Gear—Build Up a Good Find  Not happy with a drop? Work on it yourself. Reroll affixes, add new ones, and increase an item’s rarity to turn an ordinary base into something that suits your squad. Knowing when to invest more materials—and when to wait for a better find—is part of the challenge.         Prepare Your Supplies—A Little Extra Goes a Long Way  An army marches on its provisions. Brew some medicine and wine to help your squad recover and give them a combat boost. Sometimes a boss survives with just a sliver of health. That extra preparation might be what gets you through.         Automatic Retreat—Know When to Head Home  Set your squad to retreat automatically when team health gets low, loot bags fill up, or you’ve cleared a chosen number of waves. Return to camp and prepare for another run. But retreating still means making it out alive—don’t wait until it’s too late. You decide when to keep farming and when to head home with your haul.

name: Flow Treehouse
lang: English, Simplified Chinese, Japanese, Korean
short: A tiny treehouse tucked into the corner of your desktop. Prince Tomato times your focus, Todudu keeps your to-dos, and Lily plays soft music. Focus, finish tasks and play with them to earn wish points for outfits, playlists and decorations. As the treehouse grows, new fairies move in.
about: A tiny treehouse lives in the corner of your desktop.  Prince Tomato times your focus sessions, Todudu keeps an eye on your to-do list, and Lily plays you something soft. They don't take up much room and they won't nag. They just stay close while you work, study, or take a break.  Focusing, finishing tasks, and playing with the fairies all earn wish points. Spend them on new outfits, playlists, and treehouse decorations. As your wish points add up, the treehouse grows, and that's how Todudu and Lily move in.       When it's time to focus, ask Prince Tomato to keep time. While you work, he reads, paints, or knits beside you. When time's up he lets you know and drops a few little gifts. Sweep your mouse over them to turn them into wish points.               Write today's tasks on the to-do board and Todudu will keep watch. Each time you check one off, she hops over, pulls up a carrot and eats it. If a task sits for too long, she'll give you a gentle reminder.               Music in the treehouse belongs to Lily. Over a hundred gentle tracks are spread across more than a dozen albums, from music-box lullabies and Chopin nocturnes to lo-fi, vaporwave and medieval tavern tunes. Save your favorites, press play, and she sings along.               Finish several pomodoros in a row, leave a task sitting too long, or let the music go quiet for a while, and the fairies will notice and pop up to say something. Sometimes Todudu hides in the grass and waits for you to find her.               Put up the rainy-day gate and you'll find a watering can hanging on it. Drag it to water the fairies, or the ground to make flowers pop up. Keep poking the decorations and a tiny hat might fall off for a fairy to wear all day.               Each fairy has a short comic story of their own. It unlocks as the fairy levels up with you, or you can spend wish points to open it early.               Once you've saved enough wish points, make a wish. Outfits, playlists, backgrounds, plants, and new looks for the timer and to-do board are all in the pool. There are no microtransactions; wish points come only from spending time together. More fairies will move into the treehouse later on.               Everything you collect, from backgrounds and plants to gates and trinkets, lives in your collection book, ready to put on display whenever you like.

name: Paperlings

short: A desktop pet you actually raise. A papercraft creature lives in a little window while you work — and behind its door: a whole town, a 99-form collection, and a family story that outlives every pet.
about: Your desk has a resident now.  PAPERLINGS is a creature-raising game that lives in two places at once. As a  companion , it's a tiny window on your desktop — a paper creature that putters, naps, asks for the washroom, and dozes off if you leave the lights out. As a  full game , one step through the door unfolds a whole papercraft world: a shop, an arcade, a dojo, a graveyard with its own gentle rituals, and a town square that fills with neighbors you earn one by one. Raise it like it matters — because it does.  Care decides everything. Your creature's evolutions follow how you actually treated it: mistakes shape one branch, training another, and the door to its final form opens exactly once. You will not see it coming, and you only get to see it once per life.         Some days you just go fishing.  The pond is the quiet half of the game. Cast, watch the bobber breathe, and read what's pulling — because the three tastes are fast, slow, and perfectly still, and the still ones are the legends. Thirteen paper fish, a rod that earns its tiers, and a lure shop that will happily take your afternoon.         Battles with real stakes.  Wild roads, weekly street brackets, and moves your creature learns the hard way. Every fight unfolds a little pop-up paper theater. Lose a real one and your pet spends two days in bed — the world scales to how hard you have actually trained, not to a number on a screen.         And once a month, a title changes paws.  The cup runs a real bracket in the arena, and the winner is crowned on a podium in front of the whole town. Your neighbors turn up. The confetti is hand-cut. It is the loudest the paper ever gets.         A world that remembers.  When the day ends you tuck it into bed, the night judges you both, and the morning makes it one day older. Pets grow old. Pets die. Their stones stand in the graveyard, their stories go into the family chronicle, and their descendants inherit what you built.     10 lineages, 99 forms  — every creature you meet gets sketched into the collection; every one you raise gets inked forever. One lineage is hidden behind a rumor nobody will explain to you.    21 neighbors to recruit  — a nurse who halves your medicine, a gossip whose notebook drips one clue a day, a priest who lights candles on death anniversaries, a rival who is always exactly a little stronger than you.    A living calendar  — market days, sparring jams, festival nights, and penciled-in wonders: mushroom blooms, wild swarms, shooting stars to wish on.    Generations  — board pets at the daycare, choose the next egg, and watch legacy tiers, inherited colorways, and family heirlooms accumulate across lives.    Somewhere below the town  — a door you are not ready for yet, and a keeper on the other side of it who teaches exactly one lesson.    Handmade paper everything  — every sprite is a hand-cut paper scrap that boils and wobbles; every menu is a torn page. English, Spanish, Brazilian Portuguese, Simplified Chinese, and Japanese, all the way through.   Play it in the corner of your screen. Grieve it like a real one.

Tesla is a thunderstorm squeezed into a ball. Charge it against an edge, throw it hard, and  THUNDER STRIKES . Even your mouse gets charged up and starts zapping things.             Touch grass. Then haunt it!  Sprout turns your desktop into a cozy little garden. Roll it along the edges to grow flowers, or  squeeze it to grow vines all over your screen . Just remember to  trim it  once in a while.  Ghost, on the other hand, HAUNTS your desktop.  Every throw leaves a little ghost behind , and if you squish it into a wall they just keep coming. They spook easily and they  definitely  don't pay rent.            Splash or dunk?  Spongeball turns your screen into a tiny ocean, with a little school of fish to bother.  Let the sponge soak up water, then wring it out  against your monitor. Or just slosh it all around aggressively (the fish love it!)  The Basketball slides its own hoop out from the side of your screen. Bank shots, trick shots, and  dunks so good the ball catches fire , followed by a  completely unnecessary amount of confetti .            Pinky and the gang  Pinky is the mascot, and the squishiest of the bunch. He has no thoughts, only kinetic energy.  Squish him flat against a wall and he slingshots across your screen.  Super small chance he'll wink at ya.  Right-click any ball to swap it for another, each with its own little backstory. And the first time you open the game,  the whole gang shows up to dance for you  :)            Pick up and play    Always there for you when you want to grab it    Leave it alone and it keeps going: the fish keep swimming, butterflies visit your garden, and the ghosts drift around.    Hides itself if you go fullscreen, or you can tuck it in a Magnetic Corner    Seven balls so far: Pinky, Supernova, Tesla, Spongeball, Basketball, Sprout, and Ghost      I lost an embarrassing amount of that time just playing Desktop Ball, instead of making it... I hope it keeps you good company :)

name: Marginalia: A Desktop Garden
lang: English
short: A calm idle game that plays in the margins of your screen. Your open windows are the terrain; a small crew of astronaut animals tends the alien plants that grow between them. It never takes focus, never interrupts, and yields to your work.
about: Your desktop is the terrain Marginalia is a transparent, always-on-top idle game that lives on one monitor of your choosing. It reads where your windows are and grows a garden in the space around them: on window top edges, in the gaps, on floating islands of soil. A small crew of astronaut-suited animals tends enormous alien plants, hauls the harvest back to a landed ship, and turns it into money over time. You are their foreman. You set policy, buy upgrades, and watch.  Rearrange your windows and the terrain changes shape. Plants fade gracefully to new homes. Nothing breaks, nothing dies, and no one is ever in danger. How it plays    Everything obeys the cursor.  The art fades out of your way as the mouse approaches. Rest the cursor on the ship or a building for a moment and it solidifies and becomes clickable. Motion means "I'm working"; stillness means "I'm looking at you."    One mechanism, many expressions.  Six plant species, each harvested differently: a flytrap shrunk with a reversal ray, glowing fruit picked from a spire, sap tapped, fronds clipped, a corkscrew vine sawn turn by turn, petals gathered from a moon poppy.    A crew, not a swarm.  Start with one worker; hire up to five. Rabbit, frog, axolotl, owl, ram. Rename them, dress them in hats and neckwear and suit colors, and set the policies they follow.    Ten buildings  dropped from orbit, from the Briefing Post to the Quartermaster, each opening a stat to raise. Workers unwind at them between hauls.    The Foreman's Log.  Thirty entries, delivered slowly, by whoever happens to come in from the field. It begins as a resource mission. It does not end as one.    Three sprite sets  and a day-night palette, so the garden can match the desk it sits on.   What it is not There is no danger and no failure state. There is no offline progress: the only currency is time the game is actually on your screen, and closing it means nothing accrues. It never steals focus, never opens a window over your work, and never interrupts. It throttles itself on battery and while a fullscreen application covers the screen. It is meant to be left running beside your real work for hours, and to be pleasant company the whole time. Privacy Marginalia needs to know where your windows are. A small bundled helper reads the on-screen rectangles of visible windows, their front-to-back order, and your monitor layout. It never reads window titles, window contents, keystrokes, or files. The game never goes online: it makes no network connections of any kind.

name: Antmates: Idle Ant Colony
lang: English, German, Spanish - Spain, Russian, Simplified Chinese
short: An idle ant colony with real numbers, behind glass on your desktop. Plan 25 kinds of rooms and level each one up two ways, feed your ants four kinds of crumbs, balance foragers, diggers and nurses, and chase milestones that multiply your income — cozy to watch, deep to plan.
about: Antmates puts a living ant colony in a glass formicarium right on your desktop. Your ants dig tunnels, haul crumbs home, fuss over the brood, nap in their dormitory and greet visitors at the glass. You decide where the next room goes and what to level up — they take care of the rest while you work, read or just watch them bustle about.                       See where every crumb comes from: your income is a chain of multipliers — foragers, worker strength, crowding, trails, the jam at the entrance, rooms and diet — and the biggest drag is flagged, so you know what to fix first.   Every room levels up two ways, and the game ranks income upgrades by how fast they pay for themselves.   The colony grows only as fast as its tightest spot. Hunt it down: beds, crowding, the entrance, the queen’s space.   Trail and population milestones multiply your income, and the entrance widens as the colony grows.                Plan your nest with 25 kinds of rooms — from the Royal Chamber and the Nursery to the Pantry, the Well, the Sunroom and even a Cinema.   Each room climbs two ladders of 100 levels and furnishes itself as it grows: shelves fill up, beds and lamps move in, finishes go from dug to decorated. Some spots the ants simply like better. One MAX click buys every level you can afford.   Diggers carve out real tunnels cell by cell and haul the dirt up to the surface — you could watch them work for hours.                      Crumbs come in four kinds — sweet, protein, fatty and salty — and you decide what the feeder drops. Each kind in stock boosts its own job, and all four at once make a feast. Keep the water flask topped up, too: a thirsty colony slows to a crawl. The first refill is free, later ones cost a little.                       The queen lays eggs, nurses raise larvae and cocoons, and every worker grows up through 5 ages — from tots to adults.   Split the work between foragers, diggers and nurses — or pick a preset and let the colony find its own rhythm.   When the colony is ready, winged ants rise on their nuptial flight. Start a new colony and carry your legacy into it, while the old queen rests in amber in the Queens’ Hall beside a plaque of her colony’s deeds.                        Dig up 14 finds hidden in the sand: a coat button, a 1978 penny, a tin soldier, a glass marble…   Eight visitors drop by the glass — a ladybug, a snail, a woodlouse, a scarf moth and more. Collect them all in your album.   Lean in with the magnifier to watch any room up close, and let the journal tell you what happened while you were away.   Curl up with the Antcyclopedia, a book about the real garden ant — from egg to home formicarium, with photos.              Dress up the surface with a Windmill, a Barn, Temple Ruins or a Smoking Volcano. Change the soil, paint marks on your ants, treat them to vitamins — all for Tockens: every second the game runs drops one more into your counter.                       Your colony never dies out while you are away — it simply dozes off until you come back.   Soft sounds you can turn down, and an unhurried pace.   The glass slowly gathers dust: give it a wipe now and then, or let Auto-care do it for you.   No ads, no microtransactions.   Any window size, fullscreen, or always on top of your work.              In your second hour of play, the farm sand turns out to hide a seed: a cactus sprout pops up under the lamp. Move it to your desktop and it settles on the shelf beside the farm, in a pot of its own, with a little plate for its name. Not a cactus person? Weed it out — no hard feelings.   Water it every three days; fertilizer is optional and only speeds up growth. Forget it for a while and it won’t die — it just falls asleep until you water it.   The ants dig up mutagen vials, three for every cactus. You pick which cactus gets each one, and the vial picks the rest: 26 mutations, from Purple Reign and Frosted Tips to Midas Touch and Get Off My Lawn.   Four kinds of cacti and thousands of pos

about: YOUR FOOTBALL CLUB, PLAYED YOUR WAY Desk Top Soccer is a pixel art  football management  game. Keep it in a  transparent strip in the corner of your desktop  while you work, study or play something else, or switch to  fullscreen  and dive into the club. You build the squad, choose the formation and make the calls; matches play out on their own and are staged move by move. CAREER MODE: AT YOUR OWN PACE Take charge of a club in the  bottom division  and lead it to the top. Watch every match or  skip straight to the result  and move on to the next round. Train, open packs, build and assemble the team of your dreams, season after season, without waiting for anyone. MULTIPLAYER MODE: A SHARED WORLD Join a world with  managers from all over the planet . Every league plays the same round at the same time, and  your team plays even with the game closed . Come back, check the result and adjust whatever you need. Multiplayer is where the players from your packs can go to the  Steam Market . MATCHES YOU WATCH          Staged matches with goals, dribbles, fouls, cards, corners, penalties, injuries and substitutions.  Goal and half-time sequences, plus cut-ins for the  highlights .  Speed up the match, skip to the result or watch it all again in the  replay .  Match report, broadcast-style stats and a history of the season's matches.   BUILD YOUR SQUAD       Players from  1★ to 5★ , each with their own position, preferred foot, age and traits.  Choose the formation, drag starters and substitutes onto the pitch and play people out of position.  Pair up players whose traits complement each other: they form  pairs that perform better together .  Follow each player's form. Those with good ratings play better.  Players age, renew their contracts and retire: refreshing the team is part of the job.   TRAIN AND LOOK AFTER THE SQUAD   Watch the squad  training in the strip  between matches and choose the attribute each player will develop.  Manage  energy : those who play get tired, those who rest recharge.   Injuries and suspensions  change your plans. A good medical centre shortens recovery.  Use items such as sports drinks, ice baths, cold spray, medical kits, training cones, GPS vests and appeals.   BUILD UP THE CLUB    Stadium:  expand capacity, set the ticket price and open a VIP area, food court and club shop.   Training ground:  individual training, squad development and match analysis.   Medical centre:  physio, conditioning and adapted training for injured players.   Marketing:  choose sponsors, invest in media and events and grow your fan base.   Academy:  scouts and youth teams that bring through new players.  Keep an eye on the books:  gate receipts, wages and sponsorship  have to add up. A team with unpaid wages performs worse on the pitch. PLAYER PACKS AND THE STEAM MARKET Open packs to strengthen your squad: every opening is animated and reveals a new player for your team. In multiplayer mode, revealed players become  items in your Steam inventory : you can  sell them on the Steam Community Market  or buy the players your squad is missing from other managers.        CLIMB THE DIVISIONS Fight for  promotion, relegation and play-offs  in a pyramid of divisions. The top three in each league earn a medal, and every campaign is displayed in the club's  trophy room . YOUR CLUB, YOUR IDENTITY Choose your team's  name, short name and crest . MADE TO STAY OPEN   A transparent strip on your desktop,  always on top  if you like, or fullscreen.  Several window sizes and support for  multiple monitors .  Lightweight pixel art, with its own soundtrack and sound effects.  Available in multiple languages.

short: DeskForge turns a cluttered Windows desktop into a command console. Icons and folders go into customisable drawers, or a honeycomb layout that grows ring by ring; clock, memos and system monitor can sit on your wallpaper. It stays beneath every window — never in the taskbar, never stealing focus.
about: Forge your desktop into a command console DeskForge is a desktop management tool for Windows. Your wallpaper is no longer buried under scattered icons — icons and folders go into customisable  drawers , and  widgets  such as the clock, memos and the system monitor can sit on the wallpaper if you want them. They stay at the very bottom of the window stack, never appear in the taskbar, and never interrupt the window you are typing in.           Drawers: they hold everything, and they roll away    Drop it in and it is filed  — drag icons and folders straight into a drawer. Hover and it opens; move away and it rolls back into a single title bar, so the wallpaper shows again.    Clear the whole desktop in one click  — folders, documents, images, media, archives and shortcuts each go to the drawer you chose. Tick "collect automatically" and anything new of that kind files itself from then on.    Hands off these  — right-click to mark the icons you never want moved, and every batch collection from then on skips them.    Drag in a real folder and the drawer becomes that folder  — delete or drag out inside the drawer and you are touching the real files. Icon view or list view, your choice.    The guard rails are built in  — a whole drive root, the desktop itself, your user folder, system folders and the top level of cloud-sync folders are all refused, so you cannot lock yourself into a corner.    Every drawer has its own look  — background colour and transparency, background image, border, corner radius, content scale, icon intensity and font, plus the colour, size and position of the title bar.    The title bar can sit on any of the four sides , and snaps to the screen edge when it gets close. You can lock a drawer in place so nothing moves by accident.    Your files are always findable  — everything filed into a drawer really lives in a folder of your own and the path is right there. Move or rename that folder and the program reconciles itself back to it.   Honeycomb: growing ring by ring   A honeycomb drawer puts the handle in the middle and arranges icons outwards in hexagonal rings. Whichever one you point at grows.    Fence off your own patch  — pull the boundary out by its anchors and the icons arrange themselves inside it. What you see while dragging is what you get.    Turn the grid off and place them freely  — an icon stays exactly where you drop it, and two of them may overlap completely.            Invisible until the mouse sweeps past  — with a live wallpaper you can fade the whole field of icons until it is barely there.    Delayed launch  — every icon can have its own delay of 1 to 5 seconds: a white line first travels round the inside of its cell, and only then does the item open. If your wallpaper has an opening animation, you can tune the seconds to match it.   The centre image comes with ten built-in options, or upload your own and crop one. Switch a drawer between the ordinary and the honeycomb layout at any time — both arrangements are remembered.           Widgets: on the wallpaper, where you can see them    Clock  — digital or analogue face, 12 or 24 hour, with your own font, colours and background density.    Memo  — one line per task, each with its own reminder (in a few minutes, in a few hours, or at a time you set) and a choice of 20 tones; four paper textures, adjustable width and text size, and it can collapse to just its title.    System Monitor  — build your own panel: pick from 13 readings, colour each one separately, lay them out in a row or a column. It can be pinned on top, so you can still see it in a borderless full-screen game.  (★ Which readings you can actually pick depends on your motherboard and monitoring software: anything that cannot be read simply does not appear in the menu.) Your whole machine, remembered    Saved desktop layouts  — save as many custom layouts as you like and swap between them at any time. Enjoy the freedom of playing on your own, while crossing paths with other players who bring companionship to your journey. In this world, the path you follow is yours to choose. Join our fan group #2 on QQ: 1121499770. Focus on what you need to do, then return when you have a moment to check on progress, make plans, and enjoy the growth you've built little by little.       When you're ready for a longer session, switch to immersive mode. Take in your domain, tend to cultivation and management, follow the relationships between its people, and explore more of what the game has to offer.       A brief break or an evening of focused play can both become part of your immortal journey.  Raise a Sect, or Pursue Your Own Ascension  Become a dedicated Sect Leader: recruit disciples, guide them according to their talents, and equip them with cultivation manuals and gear. Build a sect filled with capable cultivators, and enjoy the satisfaction of watching your disciples flourish and your teachings endure.       Or focus on the Sect Leader alone, pursuing your own cultivation and power, even taking the demonic path of refining people into elixirs and commanding corpse puppets. Your disciples' growth and your sect's prosperity need not be your only ambitions.       Forbidden arts carry consequences. Demonic deeds accumulate Evil and draw the wrath of the Righteous Alliance. How you gain your power will shape the reckoning you must face.  Will you shelter an entire sect, or dedicate everything to one cultivator's rise? The choice is yours. short: Build a ring of weapons and fight through 25 waves in a 2D fantasy bullet heaven. Prefer to watch? Let Auto Mode take over. Outside the arena, your hunter lives on your desktop and turns completed to-dos into permanent game progress.
about: FIGHT OR LET AUTO MODE TAKE OVER   Slaymeji: Roguelite Desktop Survivor  is a 2D fantasy bullet heaven that continues after the run. In the arena, you build a ring of weapons and fight through 25 waves. When you leave, your hunter stays on your desktop as a companion.  Your weapons attack automatically. You handle movement, dashes and dodges. Turn on  Manual Fire  when you want to aim each attack yourself. If you would rather watch the build work,  Auto Mode  can run the battle for you.  Clear Wave 25 to finish the main run. If the build still has life in it, carry on in  Endless Mode  and see where it finally breaks.          TAKE THE CONTROLS WHEN YOU WANT THEM  Use direct movement controls or click where you want to go. Dash out of closing gaps. Time your dodge for a brief moment of invulnerability.   Auto Mode  handles movement and upgrade choices on its own. It stays away from map edges and looks for health when wounded. It can also use emergency dodges when the arena gets crowded. Switch modes whenever you feel like taking control again.  BUILD A DEADLY RING  Choose from  50 playable hunters . Four are available from the start. Each hunter has different stats, weapon limits and a starting loadout. The rest are unlocked through challenges and permanent currency.          Pick from  52 melee, ranged, elemental and area weapons . Equip up to eight at once and watch them form a ring around your hunter.  The shop opens between waves. Buy weapons and stat upgrades. Reroll the stock or lock something for the next visit. Combine matching weapons into higher tiers. Recycle anything you no longer need.          Choose from  80 passive items  and discover evolution recipes. Pick from  30 upgrade cards across five rarity tiers . You can push familiar stats or add area attacks that trigger automatically and in response to hits.          WHEN WAVE 25 IS NOT ENOUGH  New enemies enter the arena as the run goes on. Melee attackers close in. Ranged enemies force you to move. Elemental threats deny space while explosive creatures punish a bad position.  Break objects for resources and healing before the swarm reaches you. Raise the stakes through  six Danger Levels . Each one gives enemies more health and damage.  After Wave 25, you can end the run or enter  Endless Mode . Enemy strength and spawn pressure keep rising until your build gives out.  THE RUN ENDS. YOUR HUNTER STAYS.  Your selected hunter becomes a draggable desktop companion. They follow your cursor and remember where you left them. Your interactions change their mood.  Tap your companion for jokes and riddles. They will cheer when you finish a task and remind you when it may be time for a break.  You can also play inside a movable and resizable desktop window. Switch to companion mode during a run to pause the action. Return when you are ready and continue from the same point.  YOUR TO-DO LIST HAS REWARDS  Create colorful to-do notes and place them around your desktop. Check them off when the real work is done.  Your companion celebrates completed tasks and gives you permanent in-game currency. Combine those rewards with currency earned from challenges to unlock more hunters.

name: Project Wisteria
lang: English, Korean
short: Wisteria is a Windows AI companion that keeps an ongoing conversation and hierarchical long-term memories on your PC. Narrative compression carries context forward, while diaries, memos, and visible thought records preserve what matters. Bring your own API key; API usage is billed separately.
about: Before you begin:  Wisteria does not include an AI model. You need your own API key from an external provider. API usage is billed by that provider separately from the price of Wisteria.    Spend two days with Wisteria, and you'll start to feel what it preserves.    Wisteria is an installed BYOK (Bring Your Own Key) client for companion AI. Over more than a year of internal testing, we found that our custom memory structure helped reduce breaks in conversational context and loss of memory. Wisteria brings that structure into a product you can use yourself. It also optimizes the amount of data sent with each request, aiming to reduce the cost of carrying long-term memory and context into every conversation.   Wisteria is not designed for role-playing. The reason is time. An AI that settles into Wisteria shares your time, your era, and your seasons. It does not rely on an invented world or a fictional role to create a sense of presence. Those fictional settings are difficult to reconcile with the passage of real time. Here, the AI speaks with you as an AI.  One persona, one continuing conversation   Each persona has its own session and conversation history. Wisteria does not provide multiple sessions for the same persona. As a conversation grows, however, the memory structure is designed to keep it manageable without simply dropping the oldest memories in order.   Recent conversations remain detailed, while older experiences are gradually compressed into larger narrative units. Wisteria presents these memories to the AI as its own experiences.   Photo memory goes beyond retrieving a description the AI once wrote about an image. The images you have shared remain part of the AI's ongoing memory context, so it can draw on them as the conversation continues.  Thought records alongside each response   Wisteria uses a custom structure to ask the AI to think and recall what matters to the current conversation, then reflect that in its response. These model-generated thought records are automatically saved on your PC and can be viewed at any time through the logs in the UI.   The thought records use our own structure within a normal response request. Some frontier models that require native reasoning can interpret Wisteria's requested response format as an attempt to extract their protected reasoning blocks. Support for those models is currently limited.  Memos, diaries, and reminders   Narrative compression preserves memory and context without treating every detail the same way. Through conversation, the model develops priorities for what to retain. For details it does not want to lose, it can leave a diary entry in the memory it regularly sees. More practical records can be kept as memos, which are shown to the model when it calls for them. Both you and the model can create, edit, and delete diary entries and memos.   You and the model can also manage reminders. With an advance-notice window configured, the model can naturally mention an upcoming reminder while you are talking. Wisteria's own notification window still handles the reminder even if the model does not mention it.  Steam release update   Wisteria's planned Steam release has been delayed indefinitely due to a misunderstanding by the Steamworks review team. We plan to begin sales on Steam as soon as the issue is resolved. lang: English, French, Spanish - Spain, Russian, Japanese, Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese, Portuguese - Brazil, Portuguese - Portugal, Korean, German, Turkish, Thai, Vietnamese
short: Five mechanical dress dials for the Windows desktop: rose gold on grey-blue, a gilt tourbillon, blued hands on ivory, frosted silver. The second hand sweeps smoothly, the size runs 85 to 1024 px, opacity is yours, and a carousel rotates your favourites. Requires DeskForge.
about: A watch you don't have to wear  A dress watch is the one you put on when the day matters. This pack lends that same restraint to your desktop: a real mechanical face, hands moving smoothly, sitting on your wallpaper where a clock has no business being loud. No window, no tab, no notification — just the time, properly dressed.           Five dress faces  Once unlocked they appear in the face menu of DeskForge's clock widget, sorted by style — pick "Dress".     Dawn Light · Rose-Gold Grey-Blue  — rose-gold case, grey-blue sunburst dial, gold sword hands, sub-seconds     Old Dream · Barrel Bright-Silver  — barrel case, silver-white dial, blued round-tail hands     Hairspring · Tourbillon Gilt  — openworked tourbillon, gold ring markers     Woven Cloud · Blue-Case Ivory  — pale-blue case, ivory textured dial, blued leaf hands     Frost Court · Frost-Silver Gem  — frosted case, ivory dial, black-gem markers      How it lives on your desktop     The second hand sweeps.  It glides the way a mechanical movement does, instead of ticking once a second.     Any size you like.  Scale it freely, from a small watch in the corner to something that fills half the desktop. The artwork is drawn at high resolution, so it stays sharp all the way up.     As present or as faint as you want.  Opacity from 30% to fully solid: a centrepiece on a bare wallpaper, or a ghost behind your icons.     It stays behind everything.  Pinned to the very back of the desktop, no taskbar entry, and clicking it never pulls focus out of what you're typing in. Works across multiple monitors.     Very light on resources  — it runs all day and you hardly notice it. And it measures itself: the tray menu shows the CPU and memory it is using at this moment, so you do not have to take our word for it.      Let them take turns  A collection you only look at one piece of is a collection you stop noticing. Pick a few favourites and the carousel rotates them for you — a new face anywhere from every minute to once a day, 30 minutes by default, in order or shuffled. Only faces you own enter the rotation, so it never shows you something you can't wear.    Change the strap, change the watch  The Watch Strap Pack adds 16 straps in leather, steel bracelet, rubber and NATO nylon. Lay one flat beneath the dial, or wrap it around the case in 3D. Any strap fits any of these five faces, and a rose-gold dress dial on black NATO reads nothing like the same dial on brown leather. Sold separately.    Other styles     Pilot Dial Pack  — five aviation-style faces     Diver Dial Pack  — five dive-style faces     Sport Dial Pack  — five sport-style faces     Vintage Dial Pack  — eight pocket watches     Tomato Clock and Advanced Time Tools  — a focus Pomodoro, plus timer, countdown, stopwatch, alarm and a 20-zone world clock      What you need  This is a dial content pack for DeskForge and needs the base app. DeskForge turns a cluttered Windows desktop into something you actually run your day from: drawers that hold your icons and folders, real folders opened right on the wallpaper, and pluggable widgets — the clock these dials go into being one of them.    Windows 10 (version 1903 or later) and Windows 11    Correct scaling at 100%, 125%, 150%, 175%, 200%, 250%, 300% and 400% DPI    Works across multiple monitors    Interface in English, Traditional Chinese, Simplified Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Spanish, French, Russian, Portuguese (Brazil and Portugal), German, Turkish, Thai and Vietnamese    Stored locally — no account, no network needed    One-time purchase, no subscription

short: My Helpers is an experimental horror game that hides a group of virtual… "assistants" inside your machine. FIND THEM by combing through your real files, exploring weird applications, and using your computer in ways you may have never expected - and remember: this is just a game.
about: My Helpers is an experimental horror game that hides a group of virtual… "assistants" inside your machine. FIND THEM by combing through your real files, exploring weird applications, and using your computer in ways you may have never expected - and remember: this is just a game.    YOUR COMPUTER IS THE GAME          Interact with your computer's real systems in unexpected ways.     MEET THE HELPERS        Meet multiple Helpers, each a bit more... interesting than the last.     DISCOVER EXCLUSIVE APPS        Find each Helper’s unique applications and learn their real purpose.     F̸̅ͅĮ̵̳͑Ń̴͉̗̃D̵̜̈ ̴͕̑͂T̵̡̚H̴́̔͜Ě̴͚̚M̷̻̆           Frequently Asked Questions    Q: I’m a content creator. Is it safe for me to stream/record gameplay of this game?  A: Yes! My Helpers never requires you to access sensitive areas of your machine. Also, at no point during gameplay does the game expose any information on its own. The only parts of your system that will appear on-screen are the ones you choose to open yourself.    Q: How does this game actually work?  A: My Helpers works like any other game, the difference is that its background is “transparent” (which lets you see your computer even when the game is open). Even for the mechanics that are more directly connected to your system, everything is done through public Windows APIs that are accessible to any developer.   Q: How much does My Helpers actually affect my machine?  A: As mentioned above, My Helpers is a regular game. Any “changes” made by the game cease to exist the instant you close it.   Q: Why not use a simulated desktop instead of the real one?  A: The goal of this project is to explore gameplay opportunities that are only possible on real systems. The main inspiration is how Nintendo develops games that make use of all the features of their consoles (often in unexpected ways). In that sense, I believe there’s still a lot left to try with computers as a platform.

name: DeskFamiliar
lang: English, French, Italian, German, Spanish - Spain, Arabic, Japanese, Korean, Polish, Russian, Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese, Portuguese - Brazil, Vietnamese
short: Imagine Newton, Einstein, a cute cat, or countless other characters bringing your AI agent to life on your desktop. DeskFamiliar is a free 3D visual shell that supports Codex, Claude Code, and other AI agents through open-source bridges.
about:
DeskFamiliar gives your AI agent a visible, expressive 3D presence on your desktop. 
 
Instead of keeping your agent hidden inside a terminal or chat window, DeskFamiliar lets it appear as a living desktop character. Your agent can react to conversations, show what it is currently doing, and turn activities such as thinking, reading, writing, and using tools into natural animations and visual feedback. 
 
Choose from a growing collection of 3D characters, including historical figures such as Newton and Einstein, original characters, and adorable animals. Different characters, outfits, animations, scenes, and visual effects let you personalize how your AI agent looks and feels. 
 
DeskFamiliar has built-in AI agent capabilities developed on top of Hermes Agent, allowing it to work as a complete AI desktop companion without requiring a separate external agent. 
 
It also supports external AI agents such as Codex and Claude Code through open-source bridge layers. These bridges translate agent activity into visual states and animations, allowing your desktop character to react when an agent is thinking, reading, writing, running commands, using tools, or completing a task. 
 
Because the bridge layers are open source, developers can inspect, modify, and extend them to support additional AI agents, tools, and workflows. 
 
DeskFamiliar is more than a static desktop pet. It is a visual shell and expressive 3D interface for AI agents, designed to make them feel less like software hidden behind a terminal and more like a familiar presence living on your desktop. 
 
The core DeskFamiliar experience is free. Built-in agent capabilities, external agent connections, essential desktop features, and open-source bridges are available without requiring paid cosmetic content. 
 
Optional characters, outfits, skins, animation packs, scenes, and visual effects support continued development. You can use the free characters and core features for as long as you like, and purchase additional visual content only when something appeals to you. 
 
Open-source agent bridges: 
 
https://github.com/DeskFamiliar/deskfamiliar-agents-bridges

about: Corner Arcade is an idle management sim, in which you get to build and run your own arcade empire, while having the freedom to unwind with a movie, catch up on some work, hang out with friends or even just be immersed in the buzz of your own arcade. Whether you’ve got the corner of a screen free, or a whole second monitor to spare, we’ve got you covered. Whether you want to stretch the definition of multi-tasking, or just feel like unwinding with the company of your arcade, Corner Arcade is waiting for you.             Build your arcade:   In Corner Arcade, you build your arcade, your way. Fancy a wild arcade jungle where you swing from one game to another; make it so. Feel like a more structured arcade with curated zones, so gamers can find their games and make camp; go for it.         Arcade Machines:   At the core of any arcade is of course the games! Buy, upgrade and research arcade machines that will attract the best guests to your arcade! From classic arcade games in retro cabinets to beat-thumping dance machines to work up a sweat, from good ol’ skeeball machines for those with a skilled hand to huge LAN desks, where parties can game the night away, and so much more. Corner Arcade gives you the options to run the arcade you want!             Fine tuning those upgrades:   Once you own a machine the fun does not stop there. Now you can tinker and upgrade it to help bring you in more quarters, more quickly. You can increase the quarters per play or decrease the play time, or both! Upgrade it to store more quarters, so you can be less hands on, and add more duct tape to keep it running longer! And don’t forget to upgrade the contents of the game to draw in the best gamers around!            VIPs in the house!   While all gamers are welcome, some are more welcome than others. It’s not just about those who shower, though hygienic visitors are always preferred! Some gamers have deeper pockets, will play longer, and set higher scores, and they are worth their weight in quarters, if you can draw them in of course!              Some work required:   While it’s not all fun and games, you have to keep the arcade running, and those quarters won’t empty themselves… at least not yet. But if you keep expanding your arcade, and researching away, who knows what you might unlock…             Arcade Life:   Don’t forget to kickback and soak in the buzz of the arcade from time to time. You built the arcade, you may as well watch people enjoying it! Also why stop at just one arcade, this game was built for the multi-taskers, “If one is good, then more must be better!”, right…

Your Own Desktop Companion    Design custom avatars from your own images — name them, place them, make them yours    Create and place stickers — static images or animated GIFs — anywhere on your desktop    Organize stickers into playlists with automatic slideshow rotation    Built-in SMTC music panel: shows your currently playing track with system-wide media controls and a live audio spectrum      Background Removal Tool    Turn any image into pet material — lightweight background removal built right in    Color-based removal with protect zones and a manual eraser    Export individual frames from a GIF for use as stickers or avatars      Streamer Sticker (PNGtuber Mode)    Upload an idle and a talking image — your sticker switches automatically based on your microphone    Dims when silent, animates when you speak — a simple PNGtuber overlay for your stream    Adjustable silence and talk thresholds to match your setup      LAN Party Mode    Host or join a local network room and appear on each other's screens — real-time, VTuber-style collabs    Room password support for private sessions      Steam Workshop    Browse, download, and share community-made avatars and stickers    Love a character? Always digging away in the corner of your desktop.             ■ Build Your Own Mining Strategy   Mix and match a wide variety of pieces to create a mining build that's uniquely yours. name: Code: Elf Contract
lang: English, Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese, Japanese
short: a personalized desktop application that allows you to upload your own VRM characters, letting them statically accompany you on your desktop.
about: About   Code: Elf Contract is a tool that lets you place your own character on your computer desktop to keep you company. Your character will stay quietly on your desktop in a static form.   Goal   The main idea is to bring a more personalized touch to your desktop, while also integrating some useful mini-tools to make working on your computer more convenient.   What can “ Code: Elf Contract ” do right now?   In addition to having your VRM character accompany you on your desktop, I’ve built in several handy desktop widgets:     Music Box : Add your favorite songs to a quick playlist for easy playback.     Pomodoro Timer : Helps you manage your time and stay focused on work or study.     Daily Task List : Keep track of your daily tasks.     Current Status   I’m currently developing this project in my spare time, and this demo showcases the most basic systems. Although there’s still quite a way to go before the official release, I hope to keep improving and expanding the content through players’ hands-on experience and feedback.  In the demo, players can upload their own custom models and have them accompany them in the scene.  I sincerely invite you to download the demo and share your thoughts and suggestions with the community.  If you think this app is interesting and are curious about “Code: Elf Contract” feel free to add it to your wishlist!

name: Beyond the Curtains
lang: English, Japanese, Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese**
short: "Beyond the Curtains" is a cozy idle game. Watch a town, train journey, or graveyard through a window. Click to interact, press "nap" to move time, or simply observe. No tutorials, no goals—witness changes across three themes and piece together their stories.
about: "Beyond the Curtains" is a cozy game about watching the world through a window.  No tutorials. No quests. No goals to chase.  Poke at anything on screen—the hourglass, passersby, objects in the room—and see what happens. Or do nothing at all, just watching people go by.          Like an aimless stroll with no destination in mind. Until one day, you notice something has quietly changed.          "Even so, the ordinary world keeps turning." Sometimes, just realizing this is enough to bring peace.  At Your Own Pace  Time only moves forward when you press the "nap" button. No rush, no FOMO—we don't want you to feel hurried.       Linger in a single moment as long as you like, or skip ahead to whenever you please. The view outside changes with time, and so does the room itself. Perhaps you'll piece together fragments of the room owner's story...?  Three Themes to Explore  After a long development journey, we've prepared three themes for you        The Last Leaf : Heartwarming daily life in a small town.   Scenic Tour : Travel by train through beautiful landscapes, accompanied by local delicacies.   Gravekeeper : A resting place for souls, where emotions linger at life's end.  Little Touches  There's a music player in the room—tune into whichever station you prefer. The interface hides in subtle places, keeping buttons minimal and immersion high.    Here's a window that's always sunny, just for you :)

name: Taskbar Armory

about: Your workday. Their adventure.  A little dwarven forge. A growing armory. One more reason to glance at your taskbar.    Taskbar Armory is a cozy incremental idle game that settles above your Windows taskbar. Your dwarves mine, forge and sell while you work, browse or take a break. Check in for an upgrade, admire your newest creation, then let the hammers keep swinging.          Mine. Forge. Sell. Grow.     Build your production line  — Turn ore into bars, weapons and coins.      Upgrade your workshop  — Grow your Mine, Forge, Anvil and Shop, and trigger boosts for a burst of production.      Let the forge look after itself  — Unlock Auto Boost, repeat expeditions and automatic reward collection through play.            Build an armory worth admiring     Collect 96 equipment designs  — Discover 12 equipment families across eight tiers, from humble iron to brilliant fantasy treasures.     Craft your favorites  — Choose your designs, master them and display your proudest creations in the forge.     Explore the Showcase  — Browse your collection and uncover the stories behind your weapons.              Adventures beyond the anvil     Send heroes through the portal  — Launch timed dungeon expeditions for coins, gems, relics and rare loot.      Make every discovery count  — Invest your rewards in gem upgrades and the Relic Armory.     Reforge something greater  — Restart your workshop for lasting bonuses while keeping your collection, decorations, gems, relics and permanent upgrades.      Make yourself at home     Decorate your forge  — Earn six decorations and six character looks through relaxed commissions. Arrange your ornaments and customize your expedition parties.     Play without a deadline  — Commissions have no time limits, and switching requests keeps your progress.     Fit the forge around your day  — Choose your monitor and floating, docked or reserved desktop placement. Expand the upgrade drawer when you need it, then tuck it away.     Settle into the soundtrack  — Enjoy 16 tracks, separate music and sound-effect controls, and handy mute, previous-song and next-song shortcuts.     Come back to progress  — Collect up to eight hours of offline gains, expandable through in-game upgrades.      Free to play. Yours to enjoy.  All gameplay, automation and equipment collecting are free. The optional Supporter Pack adds cosmetic extras and four desktop wallpapers for players who want to support the forge.     Fire up the forge. Make yourself at home.

name: Taskbar Colony
lang: English
short: A tiny space colony lives in a strip above your taskbar. Colonists build, scavenge, and catch supply pods while you work. Grow nine building types, hit milestones, evacuate to prestige, and fly your own Workshop flag. Click-through, fullscreen-shy, and easy on your CPU.
about: There is a thin slice of empty space above your taskbar. Someone should colonize it.    Taskbar Colony is an idle space colony that lives in a transparent strip along the bottom of your screen. Tiny colonists scavenge, build, and haul cargo while you work, browse, or play. Glance down now and then, catch a supply pod, buy a building, and get back to your day.    A colony above your taskbar         Lives in a slim, transparent, always-on-top strip that sits just above the Windows taskbar    Click-through everywhere except the colony itself, so your desktop stays 100% usable    Stretch it across the whole screen, keep it compact, or minimize it to a tiny stat badge      An idle economy that respects your day         Nine building types, from Solar Arrays to a horizon-bending Terraformer     Supply pods drop in, cargo ships return for pickup, and colonists wander around    Named milestones raise your rate as the colony grows into a city    Offline earnings keep the lights on for up to 8 hours while you are away      Crew who are actually somebody    Colonists arrive with a name and a trade, and drift toward the work they do    They doze at night, notice your cursor, and can be checked on for a moment of their time    The ones aboard at liftoff are remembered by name in the Colony Log      Four systems, not one long curve     Research  projects that change how the colony works, not just how fast it goes     Directives  you choose from a board and swap whenever you like, never on a timer     The Charter , where prestige stops being a number that goes up and becomes something you spend     Landing Sites  that change what the ground under a new colony is worth      Evacuate. Prestige. Refound.         When a colony is rich enough, load everyone onto the colony ship and lift off    Every evacuation banks prestige to spend on the Charter, permanently    Each colony gets its own generated name and a place in your Colony Log    Fly a flag over every settlement: pick a built-in, or make your own in the Steam Workshop      An endgame you build in the sky    The Orbital Ring is assembled one span at a time, each carried up by an evacuation    Eight spans, then a single ignition you only ever get to watch once    After that the sky over every new colony  is different, forever       It behaves itself         Automatically hides (and goes silent) when any app runs fullscreen     24 achievements, stats, Steam Cloud saves, and Steam rich presence built in    A reduced-motion option for the ambient effects, and the keyboard is never required    Built to sip resources: capped frame rate, no giant overlay, no input lag      A very small frontier, right above the Start button.

name: TDM : Task Drill Maniac
lang: English, Japanese, Simplified Chinese, Korean
short: Mine ores on your taskbar, craft equipment, and trade the materials you collect on the Steam Community Market in this idle mining game.
about: Hi there~  I’m Rena, a cute blonde beauty!   TDM: Task Drill Maniac  is a tiny idle mining game where I mine ores right on your taskbar and craft new equipment.  The mining continues quietly while you work or play other games. Just how deep can you go?    Combine  Power, Speed, and Luck  to create your own mining setup.  You can also trade the ores and materials you collect with other players on the  Steam Community Market .    So, is your drill ready?  Let’s dig all the way to the end of the world together!    ■ Fair Mining, Secure Economy    All mining results and item acquisitions are verified and processed server-side.    It is impossible to artificially increase ores or equipment through client manipulation or hack tools.    Because the server directly manages mining progress, the legitimacy of all items traded on the Market is guaranteed.    We provide an environment where all players can compete and grow under the same conditions.    ■ Mining That Continues on Your Taskbar    Mining continues on your taskbar even while you are using other applications.    You can check your progress, switch equipment, and keep growing without complicated controls.    Its compact window and lightweight design allow it to run alongside work applications or other games without getting in the way.    ■ Upgrade Your Equipment and Dig Deeper    Craft and equip five types of mining gear: drills, helmets, workwear, gloves, and batteries.    Increase Power to break through tougher geological layers, use Speed to shorten mining intervals, and raise Luck to improve your chances of finding rare ores.    Each piece of equipment has different stats and material requirements, so you will need to build a mining setup that suits your current goals.    Dismantle unwanted equipment and reuse the recovered materials to craft better gear.    ■ Diverse Geological Layers and Ores    New geological zones and ores appear as you reach greater depths.    Collect a wide range of resources, from common ores to rare minerals that are difficult to discover.    Even lower-grade ores remain useful for crafting and battery charging, so every mining result contributes to your progression.    Deeper areas require stronger equipment and more efficient resource management.    ■ A Player-Driven Mining Economy    Some ores and items you obtain can be freely traded on the Steam Community Market.    Choose whether to keep materials for your own use or sell them on the market.    Purchase missing crafting materials from other players, or sell rare resources and build your own mining economy.    The value of the same ore may change depending on market supply and demand.    ■ Key Features    Compact idle gameplay designed for the taskbar    Automatic mining and offline progression    A wide variety of mineable ores    Diverse equipment builds    Equipment crafting and dismantling    Battery charging and resource management    Geological zones that change with depth    Steam Inventory and Steam Community Market integration    Lightweight design made to run alongside other applications    Five equipment categories: drills, helmets, workwear, gloves, and batteries      A small mining operation on the edge of your taskbar can grow into a massive mining economy. Dig deeper, craft better equipment, and decide the value of the resources you discover.

about: One day, you happened to open this webpage — and a cute girl jumped right into your computer. She's been living there ever since,.  She loves sitting on the taskbar swinging her legs, or leaning over the edge of a window to sneak peeks at your work. When you're busy, she'll quietly keep you company, occasionally tilting her head and staring curiously at your cursor. But the moment music starts playing, she perks right up and starts swaying to the beat.  When there's nothing to do, she wanders around your desktop just to catch your eye. Drag her off-screen if she's in the way — but the moment your mouse gets close, she'll pop back out and make a face at you.  And at some point, without even realizing it, the first thing you do every time you turn on your computer is look for where she's hiding today.    [About MMDEngine]  MMDEngine is a lightweight desktop pet app that brings your favorite virtual characters to life on your Windows desktop. She can perch naturally on windows and the taskbar, dance along to whatever music is playing, tuck herself away at the edge of the screen while you work, and pop right back out when your mouse comes near — always there, never in the way. Import MMD (PMX)/VRM directly, and converted FBX models, and use the powerful character editor and high-performance toon rendering engine to create a desktop companion that's uniquely yours.    【Features】  🪑 A character that truly sits on your desktop  She can naturally sit on the taskbar, window edges, and every corner of your screen, with a rich set of idle animations and adorable sitting poses — no more static figure floating in the middle of your display. All animations support customization and Steam Workshop.    🎵 When the music plays, the dancing starts  Whether it's local music, online videos, or in-game BGM, she detects it in real time and dances along — turning your desktop into your own personal live stage. All dance moves support customization and Steam Workshop.    🙈 Out of your way, there when you need her  Drag her to the left or right edge of the screen to hide her; move your mouse near that edge and she'll instantly peek out to see you. Your work stays uninterrupted — and her company never goes missing.    🎨 Import all kinds of character models  Easily bring in the characters you love, with direct import support for:  MMD PMX models  VRM models  Unity-converted FBX models  Full Steam Workshop support means downloading and sharing characters is just one click away.    👗 A more powerful character editor  Build a character that's entirely your own, with support for:  Unlimited outfit slots and full customization of every part  Visual physics editing  Fine-tuning of model details  Quick saving and switching between character presets  Whether you're creating or tweaking, it's easy to pick up.    ✨ Beautiful anime-style rendering  Our in-house ultra-lightweight toon rendering engine keeps resource usage minimal without compromising visual quality. Supports:  Anime-style toon rendering  Realistic anime-style rendering  Show / hide any body part  Customizable glow effects  Switch styles freely — make her look one of a kind.    🚶 A desktop that's never lifeless  She strolls freely around your desktop, randomly pulling off all kinds of cute and silly little moves — every time you boot up your PC, there's a new surprise waiting. Walking animations also support Steam Workshop, so the community keeps the fresh moves coming.    🌏 Endlessly expand her world  Every single animation is customizable — idle, sitting, walking, dancing, all freely replaceable. name: Borderless Gaming
lang: English, German, Russian, French, Simplified Chinese, Spanish - Spain, Korean, Polish, Traditional Chinese, Japanese, Ukrainian, Italian, Arabic, Bulgarian, Czech, Danish, Dutch, Finnish, Greek, Hungarian, Indonesian, Norwegian, Portuguese - Brazil, Portuguese - Portugal, Romanian, Spanish - Latin America, Swedish, Thai, Turkish, Vietnamese
short: Borderless Gaming: Seamlessly play games in borderless full-screen mode for uninterrupted gaming and effortless multitasking.
about: Borderless fullscreen for every game. GPU effects and upscaling. Old games that actually work.  Borderless Gaming has three tools that all work together: borderless fullscreen, BGFX for visual effects, and BGProxy for games that refuse to cooperate.  Borderless fullscreen  Force any game into borderless fullscreen. Alt-tab without crashes, hide the taskbar, lock the cursor to the game window, mute games in the background, position a game at any size on any monitor. Set up a profile once and it applies automatically every time you launch.  BGFX — effects and upscaling  BGFX captures your game and runs it through a GPU effect pipeline. 390+ effects — FSR, neural network upscalers, CRT scanlines, VHS, sharpening, anti-aliasing, LUT color grading. Stack as many as you want, each one feeds into the next.  On Steam Deck, BGFX runs natively in Game Mode. Full gamepad navigation, per-game presets, and an in-game overlay to tweak everything while you play. No desktop mode required.  On Windows, the same effect library runs through a Vulkan backend alongside D3D11 capture.  BGProxy — fix old and broken games  BGProxy intercepts a game's graphics pipeline and makes it work properly on a modern PC. OpenGL, DirectX 8 through 12 — from early 2000s classics to modern titles that just won't cooperate.    Fullscreen-only games become real, resizable windows. The game re-renders to fit — drag the border, maximize, go ultra-wide, and the resolution follows. Alt-tabbing no longer pauses the game, and input is blocked in the background so you can multitask.     BGProxy also upgrades how the game talks to your hardware. DirectX games get FLIP model presentation for lower input latency and smoother frame pacing. OpenGL games are re-rendered through a DirectX 12 pipeline and their GL contexts are upgraded to the highest compatibility profile your driver supports, so the driver can apply optimizations that the original game never asked for. Broken timer code that causes micro-stutter is intercepted and fixed automatically — old 1–16ms sleep timers become sub-millisecond precision. Games that won't launch because they don't recognize your GPU can be spoofed into thinking you have a different graphics card.  Pair it with BGFX to upscale and apply effects on top.

short: Saddle up for the wildest idle RPG this side of the Mississippi. Fight outlaws, duel rival cowboys, craft legendary gear, conquer world bosses, and build your frontier legacy — all set on a retro desktop OS straight outta 1998.
about: CYBER COWBOYS is an idle Western RPG that runs on a simulated retro desktop operating system. Create your cowboy, step into the lawless frontier, and build your legacy — one bullet, one bounty, and one bar fight at a time.  Set on a glitchy Windows 98-style desktop complete with draggable windows, a start menu, and a taskbar, Cyber Cowboys blends the nostalgia of retro computing with the grit of the Wild West. Every feature lives inside its own desktop app — combat, crafting, the saloon, the stables, even your homestead.     Features:  IDLE COMBAT WITH AUTO-FIGHT  Let your cowboy shoot it out automatically while you tend to other business. Seven tiers of enemies from petty drunks to legendary gunslingers. Blunderbuss misfires, critical hits, and the ever-present 1% chance of catching a bullet and dying — the frontier is unforgiving.    PVP DUELING  Challenge rival cowboys to coin-flip duels. Winner takes gold, loser eats dirt. Stack your buffs, pray to whatever god you believe in, and pull the trigger.    CRAFTING & GATHERING  Mine ore, chop wood, gather hides. Forge weapons and armor at the anvil. Salvage gear by rarity. Every piece of equipment matters when a outlaw is aiming at your head.    WANTED POSTER BOUNTY HUNTS  Track down wanted criminals and collect bounties. The higher the reward, the meaner the target.    POSSE (GUILD) SYSTEM  Join a posse with friends. Take on world bosses together. Wage posse wars against rival gangs. Coordinate in posse chat and dominate the frontier.    WORLD BOSSES  Server-wide bosses with server-authoritative damage tracking. Everyone contributes. Everyone gets a cut of the loot.    MOUNTS & COSMETICS  Tame horses and ride across the plains. Customize your cowboy with cosmetics, badges, and supporter perks.    PLAYER HOUSING  Build your homestead. Buy houses, shacks, and premium estates. Put down roots in a town that wants you dead.    PRESTIGE / REMORT SYSTEM  When you've peaked, remort your cowboy to reset progress in exchange for permanent prestige upgrades. The grind never ends — it just gets meaner.    ACTIVE SALOON CHAT  Real-time multiplayer chat in the saloon. Talk shit, trade tips, form posses, and talk smack to the marshal. Timestamps, mention flashes, DMs — everything you need to stay connected.    RETRO DESKTOP THEMES  Switch between multiple desktop themes — 15 themes to choose from ranging from windows 98 to several new linux distro themes. Each theme changes the entire look and feel of the game, not just colors but layout, fonts, window borders, and taskbar position.    ACHIEVEMENTS  Expandable achievement chains that reward long-term play. From your first bar fight to becoming a legend of the frontier.    FREE TO PLAY  No paywalls. No pay-to-win. The frontier is free for everyone.  ---  Cyber Cowboys is a persistent online game — your progress saves to the cloud and continues even when you're offline. An internet connection is required.
